title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded in San Francisco during Fourth of July celebrations when heavy traffic following a fireworks display drained their batteries faster than the system anticipated. At least a dozen vehicles required towing, and one vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks debris on the road. The system was deployed into conditions it was not designed to handle: major unplanned traffic disruptions, road closures, and the behavioral changes of a large crowd gathered for public events.

A human dispatcher monitoring traffic patterns and battery levels, or a system designed to refuse routes when congestion was forecast to exceed battery capacity, could have prevented the stranding. The deployment lacked either safeguard. Waymo acknowledged the situation and stated it is evaluating ways to improve resilience during major traffic events, but it is not established what specific changes the company intends to make or when.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations, with their batteries draining while stuck in heavy traffic following a fireworks display at the Golden Gate Bridge. Video footage verified by NBC News showed at least a dozen stationary vehicles, mostly Jaguar I-PACE models, that required towing. The company attributed the situation to major traffic disruptions, high volumes of travelers, and unplanned road closures that created unexpected congestion in the area.

Waymo stated it is evaluating ways to strengthen resilience during major traffic events. The incident included a vehicle that caught fire after driving over fireworks, though no injuries were reported. One passenger described a Waymo continuing to drive when fireworks were being set off in the road. This is not the first issue for Waymo in San Francisco, as the company briefly paused service in December after a power outage affected traffic signals. City officials said they plan to hold conversations with public and private partners to ensure smoother traffic management for future events.
